tagline: Bela Church — Century-Old Gothic Sanctuary & Underground Cave Grotto of Kasaragod

overview.short: Bela Church, formally designated as Our Lady of Sorrows Church, is a Roman Catholic church in Kasaragod district, Kerala, situated 15 km north of Kasaragod and 50 km from Mangaluru. Built in 1890, it is the oldest church in the district.
overview.description: Bela Church, formally designated as Our Lady of Sorrows Church, stands on a scenic hilltop in Bela near Badiadka, 15 km north of Kasaragod and 50 km from Mangaluru. Built in 1890 under the historic Roman Catholic Diocese of Mangalore, it is the oldest church in Kasaragod district. Acclaimed for its Gothic Revival stone architecture, ornate sanctuary, tall bell tower, and a unique 300-metre subterranean tunnel cave grotto, the church is a prominent pilgrimage landmark celebrated for its annual feast and rich centenary heritage.

topPlaces.name: Neerchal Cultural Heritage
topPlaces.description: Neerchal is a charming rural heritage village in Kasaragod district situated just 1 km from Bela Church. Known for its traditional agricultural landscapes, ancestral manors, and vibrant local cultural harmony.

image.alt: Panoramic view of Neerchal village landscape near Kasaragod

topPlaces.travelTime: ~5 mins walk / 2 mins drive from Bela Church

topPlaces.name: Seethangoli & Naikap Hills
topPlaces.description: Seethangoli is an elevated semi-urban village connecting northern Kasaragod with the interior highlands. Surrounded by green valleys, historic shrines, and pleasant viewpoints overlooking arecanut plantations.

image.alt: Holy Family Church architecture in Kumbla near Seethangoli

topPlaces.name: Ananthapura Lake Temple
topPlaces.description: Ananthapura Lake Temple is the only lake temple in Kerala, situated in the center of a serene rectangular lake in Kasaragod. Dating back to the 9th century, it is the original seat (Moolasthanam) of Anantha Padmanabha Swamy and famous for its legendary vegetarian lake crocodile.

image.alt: Ananthapura Lake Temple surrounded by sacred waters in Kasaragod

topPlaces.name: Mallikarjuna Temple, Kasaragod
topPlaces.description: The historic Mallikarjuna Temple is one of the most prominent Shiva temples in Kasaragod town. Believed to have been consecrated by the legendary sage Ikshvaku, it is renowned for its annual festival and Yakshagana performances.

image.alt: Mallikarjuna Temple entrance and gabled roof in Kasaragod

topPlaces.name: Kumbla Coastal Town & Estuary
topPlaces.description: Kumbla is a historic coastal port and former seat of the Kumbla Rajas along the Arabian Sea. It features scenic backwater estuaries, ancient bridges, and coastal village life fringed by coconut palm groves.

image.alt: Scenic view of Kumbla estuary and coastline in Kasaragod

topPlaces.name: Chandragiri Fort & River Estuary
topPlaces.description: Built in the 17th century by Shivappa Nayaka of Bednore, Chandragiri Fort occupies a high vantage point overlooking the confluence of the Chandragiri River with the Arabian Sea. Its weathered laterite bastions offer panoramic sunset views.

image.alt: Chandragiri Fort laterite stone ramparts overlooking the river

topPlaces.name: Bekal Fort & Coastal Ramparts
topPlaces.description: Bekal Fort is the largest and most magnificent sea fort in Kerala, spreading across 40 acres of seaside headland in Kasaragod. Famous for its keyhole-shaped layout, soaring observation tower, underground water tank, and crashing waves against its ramparts.

image.alt: Sweeping view of Bekal Fort bastions along the Arabian Sea

topPlaces.name: Ranipuram Hills & Shola Vistas
topPlaces.description: Known as the 'Ooty of Kerala', Ranipuram is Kasaragod's highest hill resort situated at 750 m altitude along the Western Ghats. It boasts evergreen shola forests, monsoon mist trails, and rolling grassy peaks ideal for nature trekking.

image.alt: Panoramic grassy mountain slopes and shola woods at Ranipuram

topPlaces.travelTime: ~1 hr 15 mins drive from Bela Church
